granule_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
granule_volume_fraction.rationale: One table, one method, one paper, which is what makes the 77-fold spread across these cells a comparison rather than four unrelated numbers. Table 2 as printed, which is an OVERESTIMATE: the paper's Appendix puts the bias from finite section thickness at up to 44% for this cell, so the true fraction is between 0.0014 and 0.0020. Not corrected here because the Appendix states a maximum rather than a point estimate.

microvillus_density_per_um2.conditions: Resting primary human peripheral blood T cells, live and unfixed; variable-angle TIRF with 3D surface reconstruction
microvillus_density_per_um2.rationale: 3 +/- 0.5 per um^2. Independently the midpoint of the 2-4 range from SEM morphometry across lymphocyte sources two decades earlier (PMID 15130947) -- two labs, two unrelated methods, the same number. Measured on LIVE cells, so it escapes the critical-point-drying artefact; the same paper's own SEM gives 4.5, which is the size of that artefact.
microvillus_density_per_um2.source: Jung Y et al., PNAS 2016, Fig. S2 legend

microvillus_diameter_um.conditions: Resting primary human T cells; SEM. Effector T cells measured 'comparable' in the same paper
microvillus_diameter_um.rationale: Midpoint of a measured 70-100 nm range; the measurement is the range. The 150 nm figure in circulation traces to a review and could not be confirmed in any primary source.

microvillus_length_um.rationale: A MEDIAN of a strongly right-skewed distribution, not a mean. Lengths run 'from 0.1 um to several micrometers' (PMID 27647916, verbatim), so a constant-length coat has the wrong shape and not merely the wrong number. Confirmed from an unrelated direction by PMID 6775712, read 2026-10-20: TEM morphometry puts 'the height of the membrane foldings at 305 mosmole' at 'about 0.35 um', and checks it by arithmetic -- a 6.72 um smooth-sphere diameter plus twice the folding height gives 7.42 um, which is what light microscopy measures at the outer edge. Two methods 24 years apart, one measuring villus length and the other folding height, agree to two figures.

nuclear_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
nuclear_volume_fraction.rationale: The record reads 'nucleus 44.4%: granules 0.2%: mitochondria 3.8%: cytoplasm 51.6%'. Petrzilka (PMID 308396) agrees independently at 0.458, from 47.5 um^3 of nucleus in a 103.8 um^3 cell. A RADIUS is the cube root of this; using the fraction as a radius gives a nucleus at 8.8% of the cell. The same Appendix that discounts the granule fractions clears this one: the section-thickness error is 'negligible, because the section thickness is small in comparison to nuclear dimensions'. Checked against the paper's own Table 1, where an eosinophil nucleus of 37 um^3 in a 206 um^3 cell is 18.0% against Table 2's 17.9%.

microvillus_length_um.rationale: A MEDIAN of a strongly right-skewed distribution, not a mean. Lengths run 'from 0.1 um to several micrometers' (PMID 27647916, verbatim), so a constant-length coat has the wrong shape and not merely the wrong number. Confirmed from an unrelated direction by PMID 6775712, read 2026-10-20: TEM morphometry puts 'the height of the membrane foldings at 305 mosmole' at 'about 0.35 um', and checks it by arithmetic -- a 6.72 um smooth-sphere diameter plus twice the folding height gives 7.42 um, which is what light microscopy measures at the outer edge. Two methods 24 years apart, one measuring villus length and the other folding height, agree to two figures.

nuclear_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
nuclear_volume_fraction.rationale: The record reads 'nucleus 44.4%: granules 0.2%: mitochondria 3.8%: cytoplasm 51.6%'. Petrzilka (PMID 308396) agrees independently at 0.458, from 47.5 um^3 of nucleus in a 103.8 um^3 cell. A RADIUS is the cube root of this; using the fraction as a radius gives a nucleus at 8.8% of the cell. The same Appendix that discounts the granule fractions clears this one: the section-thickness error is 'negligible, because the section thickness is small in comparison to nuclear dimensions'. Checked against the paper's own Table 1, where an eosinophil nucleus of 37 um^3 in a 206 um^3 cell is 18.0% against Table 2's 17.9%.

granule_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
granule_volume_fraction.rationale: One table, one method, one paper, which is what makes the 77-fold spread across these cells a comparison rather than four unrelated numbers. Table 2 as printed, which is an OVERESTIMATE: the paper's Appendix puts the bias from finite section thickness at up to 44% for this cell, so the true fraction is between 0.0014 and 0.0020. Not corrected here because the Appendix states a maximum rather than a point estimate.

granule_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
granule_volume_fraction.rationale: One table, one method, one paper, which is what makes the 77-fold spread across these cells a comparison rather than four unrelated numbers. Table 2 as printed, which is an OVERESTIMATE: the paper's Appendix puts the bias from finite section thickness at up to 44% for this cell, so the true fraction is between 0.0014 and 0.0020. Not corrected here because the Appendix states a maximum rather than a point estimate.

microvillus_density_per_um2.conditions: Resting primary human peripheral blood T cells, live and unfixed; variable-angle TIRF with 3D surface reconstruction
microvillus_density_per_um2.rationale: 3 +/- 0.5 per um^2. Independently the midpoint of the 2-4 range from SEM morphometry across lymphocyte sources two decades earlier (PMID 15130947) -- two labs, two unrelated methods, the same number. Measured on LIVE cells, so it escapes the critical-point-drying artefact; the same paper's own SEM gives 4.5, which is the size of that artefact.
microvillus_density_per_um2.source: Jung Y et al., PNAS 2016, Fig. S2 legend

microvillus_diameter_um.conditions: Resting primary human T cells; SEM. Effector T cells measured 'comparable' in the same paper
microvillus_diameter_um.rationale: Midpoint of a measured 70-100 nm range; the measurement is the range. The 150 nm figure in circulation traces to a review and could not be confirmed in any primary source.

microvillus_length_um.rationale: A MEDIAN of a strongly right-skewed distribution, not a mean. Lengths run 'from 0.1 um to several micrometers' (PMID 27647916, verbatim), so a constant-length coat has the wrong shape and not merely the wrong number. Confirmed from an unrelated direction by PMID 6775712, read 2026-10-20: TEM morphometry puts 'the height of the membrane foldings at 305 mosmole' at 'about 0.35 um', and checks it by arithmetic -- a 6.72 um smooth-sphere diameter plus twice the folding height gives 7.42 um, which is what light microscopy measures at the outer edge. Two methods 24 years apart, one measuring villus length and the other folding height, agree to two figures.

nuclear_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
nuclear_volume_fraction.rationale: The record reads 'nucleus 44.4%: granules 0.2%: mitochondria 3.8%: cytoplasm 51.6%'. Petrzilka (PMID 308396) agrees independently at 0.458, from 47.5 um^3 of nucleus in a 103.8 um^3 cell. A RADIUS is the cube root of this; using the fraction as a radius gives a nucleus at 8.8% of the cell. The same Appendix that discounts the granule fractions clears this one: the section-thickness error is 'negligible, because the section thickness is small in comparison to nuclear dimensions'. Checked against the paper's own Table 1, where an eosinophil nucleus of 37 um^3 in a 206 um^3 cell is 18.0% against Table 2's 17.9%.

lethal_contact_minutes.conditions: Human: healthy-donor HLA-A2.1+ CD8+ T cells transduced with the F5 anti-MART1 TCR, killing HLA-matched MART1+ M202 melanoma cells; live-cell interferometry. "Individual cytotoxic events due to recognition of CTLs are confirmed by a characteristic decrease in target cell mass following prolonged contact (30 min to 2 h) with a corresponding CTL."
lethal_contact_minutes.rationale: Midpoint of the reported 30 min to 2 h range of contact preceding target death. Consistent with mouse measurements: a 75.7 +/- 8.3 min mean lethal-synapse duration for OT-I CTLs on B16F10 cells (PMID:37500886) and 1.8 +/- 1.5 h from binding to death on MEC-1/OVA cells (PMID:34471116).
lethal_contact_minutes.source: Zangle TA et al., PLoS One 2013 (PMC3720853)

lytic_granule_count.rationale: 63 +/- 23. Explicitly NOT the 194-206 the same paper reports for the NK-92 and YTS lines, which is what reviews quote as 'almost 200 granules': immortalised lines carry about three times the load.

lytic_granule_diameter_um.rationale: 251 +/- 2 nm, where the +/- is a standard error and carries no spread information. Bracketed by two other methods: 333 +/- 103 nm by STED on NK-92 (PMID 21931536), and a 3.3 fF capacitance step on primary human CD8 T cells (PMID 26296096) which at 10 fF/um^2 works out at 324 nm.

Independently the midpoint of the 2-4 range from SEM morphometry across lymphocyte sources two decades earlier (PMID 15130947) -- two labs, two unrelated methods, the same number. Measured on LIVE cells, so it escapes the critical-point-drying artefact; the same paper's own SEM gives 4.5, which is the size of that artefact.

microvillus_diameter_um.conditions: Resting primary human T cells; SEM. Effector T cells measured 'comparable' in the same paper
microvillus_diameter_um.rationale: Midpoint of a measured 70-100 nm range; the measurement is the range. The 150 nm figure in circulation traces to a review and could not be confirmed in any primary source.

microvillus_length_um.rationale: A MEDIAN of a strongly right-skewed distribution, not a mean. Lengths run 'from 0.1 um to several micrometers' (PMID 27647916, verbatim), so a constant-length coat has the wrong shape and not merely the wrong number. Confirmed from an unrelated direction by PMID 6775712, read 2026-10-20: TEM morphometry puts 'the height of the membrane foldings at 305 mosmole' at 'about 0.35 um', and checks it by arithmetic -- a 6.72 um smooth-sphere diameter plus twice the folding height gives 7.42 um, which is what light microscopy measures at the outer edge. Two methods 24 years apart, one measuring villus length and the other folding height, agree to two figures.

nonlethal_contact_minutes.conditions: Mus musculus: virus-specific CTLs in lymph node, two-photon intravital imaging. "Individual contacts between CTLs and surviving targets lasted 8.5 min (Figure 4F), and individual contacts between CTLs and killed targets lasted for approximately 9.0 min (median; Figure 4F)."
nonlethal_contact_minutes.rationale: Median non-lethal contact of mouse CTLs in vivo, used for the human row because no human measurement was found. In vivo imaging of mouse melanoma gives a median of 15 min for the transient, non-lethal contacts that make up >95% of CTL contacts there (PMID:34471116).

nuclear_volume_fraction.conditions: Human peripheral blood lymphocyte; stereology on electron micrographs
nuclear_volume_fraction.rationale: The record reads 'nucleus 44.4%: granules 0.2%: mitochondria 3.8%: cytoplasm 51.6%'. Petrzilka (PMID 308396) agrees independently at 0.458, from 47.5 um^3 of nucleus in a 103.8 um^3 cell. A RADIUS is the cube root of this; using the fraction as a radius gives a nucleus at 8.8% of the cell. The same Appendix that discounts the granule fractions clears this one: the section-thickness error is 'negligible, because the section thickness is small in comparison to nuclear dimensions'. Checked against the paper's own Table 1, where an eosinophil nucleus of 37 um^3 in a 206 um^3 cell is 18.0% against Table 2's 17.9%.

Conjugation is scored as "the NK cell assumes a rounded morphology with membrane flattening at the site of intercellular contact", distinct from a following "attachment" phase in which it "remains attached to the target cell but visibly seeks to migrate away". "On average, activated NK cells remained conjugated to target cells twice as long (65 vs. 29 min, p < 0.005) ... as resting NK cells."
nonlethal_contact_minutes.rationale: The 29 min is the mean conjugation of RESTING NK cells, which in this assay "showed a significantly lower ability to kill HEK293T cells than activated cells" -- so their conjugations are predominantly the non-lethal ones, which is the quantity wanted. It is the committed conjugate, not any touch: a study scoring contact as bare co-localization of the two cells reports most NK-target interactions as transient, under 4 min (PMID:27323411), and those brushes are encounters a simulation filters out at recognition rather than contacts it times. Longer than the 19 min lethal contact, as expected -- a synapse that fails to kill is the more stable one (perforin-null CTL synapses persist for hours, PMID:37500886). In 3D collagen the comparable activated-NK figure is 47.9 min against 65 min in 2D (PMID:31337806), so a value in tissue is likely somewhat lower than this 2D one.
